decision: probed the machine for toolchain and model credentials before planning anything
why: did not want to design against assumptions about what was installed
evidence: powershell probe of node/npm/bun/git/gh/python and env vars
result: no node on PATH, no LLM key of any kind, git and gh and python present

decision: tested the gh token against GitHub Models instead of assuming it would work
why: whether a credential works is measurable, so measuring beat guessing
evidence: live call to models.github.ai catalog and inference endpoints
result: both returned HTTP 410, GitHub Models was retired 2026-07-30, path permanently closed

decision: found node was already installed rather than missing
why: winget said the package existed, so the real problem was a stale PATH not a missing install
evidence: winget list OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS, node --version after prepending the dir
result: node 24.19.0 and npm 11.17.0 work, every node command must prepend the winget portable dir

decision: treated the dev box and the production host as different hardware
why: dev here has no GPU at all, production is a 4090 with 24GB, so a GPU-dependent test suite would be unrunnable locally
evidence: Win32_VideoController shows only Hyper-V Video, nvidia-smi absent
result: engine tests must run against a deterministic fake DM, real model smoke-tested separately

decision: made a bootstrap commit on main so feature worktrees could exist
why: a brand new repo has no HEAD, and worktrees need one
result: main has a root commit, .worktrees/ is gitignored

decision: created the feature worktree and did all work there
why: house rule is that the primary checkout is never edited directly
result: worktree live, primary root resolves correctly from inside it

decision: built a model probe before designing the DM contract
why: the contract depends on whether a local model can be trusted to emit valid actions, and that is a number not an opinion
result: probe runs three decoding modes and validates against real engine invariants

decision: measured three decoding modes against a real local model
why: wanted the comparison against a baseline rather than just testing the mode I expected to win
evidence: probe output, 8 trials each on qwen2.5:3b-instruct

decision: rejected plain JSON mode despite it parsing on every trial
why: it parsed 8/8 and was still wrong 8/8, emitting capital-N Narration and no intent at all
result: a parse-only gate would have scored it perfect, so the gate had to check shape not syntax

decision: split model failure into two classes and only claimed one was solved
why: constrained decoding fixes shape, it cannot stop a schema-valid action from being rules-illegal
result: engine still owns rules validation, that is now the only place model output can be rejected

decision: dropped the transpiler and test framework from the plan
why: node 24 runs .ts directly and node --test handles .ts, so ts-node and jest and vitest all earn nothing
evidence: ran a .ts file and a .ts test directly, both passed
result: API tier and engine tests need zero build tooling

decision: sent the DM contract to four competing designs instead of picking one
why: it is a one-way door, and a wrong call here means either a DM that hallucinates HP or a DM that cannot improvise
evidence: four background runners on claude-opus-5, gpt-5.6-sol, grok-4.5, gemini-3.8-flash

decision: pushed the probe result to the running candidates mid-flight
why: they were designing a parse-repair ladder for a problem the runtime already eliminates
